calls.head: Top line on top line: Suzuki vs. MacKinnon
calls.body: At home, the Canadiens keep sending Suzuki’s line (Caufield, Suzuki and Slafkovský) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Martin St. Louis has been choosing strength on strength. Tonight the Avalanche’s first line is Lehkonen, MacKinnon and Nečas.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Burns plays his 1,600th game as the Avalanche beat the Canadiens
paras: Fedor Svechkov got the scoring started for the Avalanche early in the first, and Brock Nelson extended the lead to 2-0 late in the period. Nick Suzuki got the Canadiens on the board midway through the second, but that was as close as they got. Artturi Lehkonen made it 3-1 for the Avalanche on the power play early in the third, and Nicolas Roy added an empty-net goal with 13 seconds left to make it 4-1.

The Avalanche had a bit more of the good stuff. Mackenzie Blackwood made 25 saves for the Avs, and Jakub Dobeš stopped 23 of 26 at the other end. Blackwood has earned a point in eight straight starts (7-0-1). The Avalanche improved to 12-6-3, third in the Central, while the Canadiens fell to 12-4-4, second in the Atlantic.

items.text: The Canadiens’ twelve-game point streak is over.
The Avalanche have points in five straight games (3-0-2).
Cole Caufield has a point in six straight games.
Nick Suzuki extended his point streak against Colorado to seven games.
